Option B is more likely. This rests on clinical reasoning, not on a causal test of the data.

The data show the two labels are associated. Among patients with R Ischias, 57% (321 of 563) also have R L5 radiculopathy. Among patients without it, 44% (6,919 of 15,821) do. A table of co-occurrence can't show which label drives the other.

Clinically, sciatica (Ischias) is a symptom. It is usually caused by compression or irritation of a lumbosacral nerve root, and L5 is one of the roots most often involved. So the root lesion (L5 radiculopathy) causes the sciatica, not the other way round.

ANSWER: B
